mainClaim: Government regulation of social media content threatens free speech and innovation more than it protects users
evidence: No verified source is cited for this argument. The argument rests on reasoning: compliance costs fall hardest on small platforms, and vague definitions of harmful content give governments room to suppress lawful speech.
supportingPoints: Content moderation at scale with 100% accuracy is technically impossible
Regulatory definitions of 'harmful content' are vague and politically manipulable
Encryption backdoors required by some proposals compromise all user security
Competition and user choice more effective than government mandates
limitations: The earlier Digital Services Act removal and compliance-cost figures could not be traced to a published source and were removed. Other figures in the supporting points have not been checked. Acknowledges harms exist but questions regulatory solutions. Doesn't fully address child safety concerns. May underweight coordination problems requiring collective action. Alternative solutions not fully developed.
